**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image features:**
- Mature corn field, low-angle canopy shot
- Main leaf shows mottled yellow-orange-green pattern, reddish-brown at margins/edges
- Background leaves show varying yellowing/browning
- No distinct large lesions (rules out NCLB, Gray_leaf_spot, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight)
- No discrete white/black spots (rules out Tar_spot, Holcus_spot, Eyespot which shows discrete circular yellow-haloed spots)
- No distinct pustule clusters (Common_rust pustules appear more scattered/brick-red)

**Key comparison:**
- **Southern_rust**: Dense orange-yellow pustules mainly on upper surface. When severe, gives leaves an overall orange/rusty mottled appearance — matches the test image's general yellowish-orange mottling
- **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: More streaky/veinal pattern
- **Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma**: Would show more purple/reddish discoloration and stunting
- **Eyespot**: Shows more distinct round circular spots — not matching the diffuse pattern

The overall rusty-orange mottled coloring of mature corn leaves, viewed at canopy level, is most consistent with **Southern_rust** (Puccinia polysora), where dense pustules on the upper leaf surface create this diffuse orange-yellow appearance.
